II-8, and II-9) indicate a divide traversing the tract from the south-\neast corner to the northwest corner. East of this divide, flow is to
the north and northeast to East Fork of Sarpy Creek. West of the divide,
flow is westward to Sarpy Creek and its tributaries. The flow is radially away from small topographic and potentiometric highs in the Robinson
coal aquifer in the southwest corner of Tract III.
Flow through the upper part of the shallow system discharges to springs and seeps at the base of the coal beds, clinker and more permeable sandstone units. The system discharges to the alluvium and either to the creeks or through the alluvium to the lower part of the shallow flow system.
In the lower parts of the shallow flow systems, the flow is to the northward to discharge points near the Yellowstone River (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1). The lower part of the shallow flow system is recharged in part from local precipitation, from lateral flow from the southeast, and possibly from the base of the alluvium in Sarpy and East Fork Sarpy Creek valleys (as suggested by water levels in the alluvium that are below the levels of nearby stream channels) (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1).
